What sets us apart

Safe, busy, and properly adventurous.

“We strive to provide a safe and fun environment in which kids have opportunities to grow into our world's next leaders.” That's Meg's line, and it's the whole program.

Licensed by Washington DCYF

A licensed school-age program since 2013, for up to 45 kids ages 5–12 — the same standards every licensed center in the state is held to.

Brightwheel, every day

Sign in and out, message the staff, and pay — all in the app most Enumclaw parents already have on their phone.

Breakfast and snack, included

Breakfast in the morning and a healthy snack after school, in every plan. Nothing extra to pack at 6:30 am.

Break days are field-trip days

No school? Everyone's on the bus. Museums, hikes, the rink, the pool — the trips regulars talk about all year.

Northwest TrekChildren's MuseumIce skatingSwimmingHikingFun Center

    Meet Meg

    She planned this program before she had a building.

    Meg fell for before-and-after-school care working at the Ferndale and Bellingham Boys & Girls Clubs while she was at Western.

    She graduated with a BA in Human Services specializing in school-age program management, returned to Enumclaw, and ran programs for the Salvation Army and the YMCA. When Cedar River Academy offered her a home for her own program in 2012, she opened Enumclaw Adventures within two weeks.

    The idea hasn't changed since: a safe, fun place where kids lead. Fifth graders are promoted to Junior Staff and show the new kids the ropes, and everyone earns Be-Great-Bucks for doing their part — then spends them at the Be-Great-Store.

      Drop off from 6:30 am, or we'll grab them at the bell. Breakfast or snack is waiting.
